prs.title: fix: buffer stdio server writes during progress notifications
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs address the same root cause: stdio_server creates its read/write anyio memory object streams with buffer size 0 (a strict rendezvous channel), which causes a sender (e.g. a handler emitting a progress notification followed immediately by its final response) to block until the paired receiver (stdout_writer) is ready for that exact message — producing stalls/blocking behavior in the stdio transport. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs address the same root cause: stdio_server creates its read/write anyio memory object streams with buffer size 0 (a strict rendezvous channel), which causes a sender (e.g. a handler emitting a progress notification followed immediately by its final response) to block until the paired receiver (stdout_writer) is ready for that exact message — producing stalls/blocking behavior in the stdio transport. prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2654 fixes the bug by default: it bumps the write_stream buffer from 0 to 1 directly in stdio_server with no API change required, includes an inline comment stating the rationale (a handler queuing its final response while stdout_writer is still flushing an earlier progress notification), and adds a new BlockingStdout test fixture in test_stdio.py that reproduces the blocking scenario end-to-end. #2215 instead adds two new keyword parameters (read_stream_buffer_size, write_stream_buffer_size) but leaves both defaults at 0 — so the underlying blocking behavior is unchanged out of the box and only resolved if a caller explicitly opts in by passing a nonzero size, making it a less direct fix for the same defect. Both PRs touch the identical two lines creating read_stream/write_stream in stdio.py, so merging both as-is would conflict.

prs.title: fix(server): reject concurrent duplicate JSON-RPC request ids
prs.author: arimu1
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Concurrent requests reusing the same JSON-RPC request id overwrite each other's slot in `_request_streams`, cross-wiring responses (one request gets the other's payload, the other hangs). Both PRs add a check to reject a duplicate in-flight request id with an error response. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Concurrent requests reusing the same JSON-RPC request id overwrite each other's slot in `_request_streams`, cross-wiring responses (one request gets the other's payload, the other hangs). Both PRs add a check to reject a duplicate in-flight request id with an error response. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3063 keys `_request_streams` by `str(message.id)`, which collapses the JSON-RPC-legal distinction between integer id `1` and string id "1" (a numeric id can false-positive against an in-flight string id, or vice versa cross-wire) and doesn't guard against a string id equal to the reserved `GET_STREAM_KEY` sentinel ("_GET_stream"), which would collide with the standalone GET stream slot. #3221 replaces the plain str() cast with a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` (prefixing `i:`/`s:`) that keeps int and string ids distinct and can never equal `GET_STREAM_KEY`, fixing the same race without those two edge-case bugs.

prs.title: fix(oauth): avoid lock contention for long-running requests
prs.author: ctaylor86
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: context.lock in async_auth_flow is held for the full duration of the outgoing HTTP request, not just for token acquisition/refresh, so one long-running request through an OAuthClientProvider blocks every other concurrent request sharing that provider. (3 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: context.lock in async_auth_flow is held for the full duration of the outgoing HTTP request, not just for token acquisition/refresh, so one long-running request through an OAuthClientProvider blocks every other concurrent request sharing that provider. (3 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3252 and #2858 both narrow the critical section by moving `response = yield request` outside the `async with self.context.lock` block, but keep a single anyio.Lock. #3243 replaces that lock with two anyio.Semaphore(1, max_value=1) instances (one for the provider, one flow_lock for refresh/authorization transitions), with an inline comment explaining this is needed because anyio.Lock requires release by the same task that acquired it, while httpx can resume or close the auth-flow generator from a different task than the one that yielded it - a failure mode the simpler single-lock narrowing in #3252 and #2858 does not address.

prs.title: fix(shared): make UrlElicitationRequiredError pickle-safe
prs.author: ulofiai
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: MCPError (specifically UrlElicitationRequiredError, and by extension other subclasses like NoBackChannelError) is not pickle-safe: the default Exception.__reduce_ex__ reconstructs via cls(*self.args), but self.args is set by MCPError.__init__ to (code, message, data), which doesn't match subclass constructor signatures like UrlElicitationRequiredError(elicitations, message=None) — raising TypeError on every unpickle (tracked as #2431). (3 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: MCPError (specifically UrlElicitationRequiredError, and by extension other subclasses like NoBackChannelError) is not pickle-safe: the default Exception.__reduce_ex__ reconstructs via cls(*self.args), but self.args is set by MCPError.__init__ to (code, message, data), which doesn't match subclass constructor signatures like UrlElicitationRequiredError(elicitations, message=None) — raising TypeError on every unpickle (tracked as #2431). (3 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: 3262 fixes __reduce__ once on the MCPError base class using MCPError.__new__(error_type) + Exception.__init__(restored, *args) plus a restored __dict__, so every current and future subclass round-trips through pickle without any per-subclass code — its test file was updated to import and exercise NoBackChannelError alongside UrlElicitationRequiredError, confirming the generic path. 2555 adds __reduce__ only on UrlElicitationRequiredError itself (reconstructing from self._elicitations/self.message), so other MCPError subclasses such as NoBackChannelError remain unpicklable since they still fall through to the default cls(*self.args) path. 2478 also attempts a base-class-level fix but round-trips each subclass through its from_error_data/from_error classmethod with a special case for UrlElicitationRequiredError — that path only reconstructs fields exposed via ErrorData and could drop instance attributes set outside of it, and the posted diff never shows the __reduce__ hookup that would actually call the new _restore_mcp_error helper, leaving it unverified as wired in.

clusters.pick_reason: #3252 and #2858 both narrow the critical section by moving `response = yield request` outside the `async with self.context.lock` block, but keep a single anyio.Lock. #3243 replaces that lock with two anyio.Semaphore(1, max_value=1) instances (one for the provider, one flow_lock for refresh/authorization transitions), with an inline comment explaining this is needed because anyio.Lock requires release by the same task that acquired it, while httpx can resume or close the auth-flow generator from a different task than the one that yielded it - a failure mode the simpler single-lock narrowing in #3252 and #2858 does not address.

clusters.pick_reason: #3063 keys `_request_streams` by `str(message.id)`, which collapses the JSON-RPC-legal distinction between integer id `1` and string id "1" (a numeric id can false-positive against an in-flight string id, or vice versa cross-wire) and doesn't guard against a string id equal to the reserved `GET_STREAM_KEY` sentinel ("_GET_stream"), which would collide with the standalone GET stream slot. #3221 replaces the plain str() cast with a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` (prefixing `i:`/`s:`) that keeps int and string ids distinct and can never equal `GET_STREAM_KEY`, fixing the same race without those two edge-case bugs.

clusters.pick_reason: 3262 fixes __reduce__ once on the MCPError base class using MCPError.__new__(error_type) + Exception.__init__(restored, *args) plus a restored __dict__, so every current and future subclass round-trips through pickle without any per-subclass code — its test file was updated to import and exercise NoBackChannelError alongside UrlElicitationRequiredError, confirming the generic path. 2555 adds __reduce__ only on UrlElicitationRequiredError itself (reconstructing from self._elicitations/self.message), so other MCPError subclasses such as NoBackChannelError remain unpicklable since they still fall through to the default cls(*self.args) path. 2478 also attempts a base-class-level fix but round-trips each subclass through its from_error_data/from_error classmethod with a special case for UrlElicitationRequiredError — that path only reconstructs fields exposed via ErrorData and could drop instance attributes set outside of it, and the posted diff never shows the __reduce__ hookup that would actually call the new _restore_mcp_error helper, leaving it unverified as wired in.

clusters.pick_reason: #3252 and #2858 both narrow the critical section by moving `response = yield request` outside the `async with self.context.lock` block, but keep a single anyio.Lock. #3243 replaces that lock with two anyio.Semaphore(1, max_value=1) instances (one for the provider, one flow_lock for refresh/authorization transitions), with an inline comment explaining this is needed because anyio.Lock requires release by the same task that acquired it, while httpx can resume or close the auth-flow generator from a different task than the one that yielded it - a failure mode the simpler single-lock narrowing in #3252 and #2858 does not address.

clusters.pick_reason: #3063 keys `_request_streams` by `str(message.id)`, which collapses the JSON-RPC-legal distinction between integer id `1` and string id "1" (a numeric id can false-positive against an in-flight string id, or vice versa cross-wire) and doesn't guard against a string id equal to the reserved `GET_STREAM_KEY` sentinel ("_GET_stream"), which would collide with the standalone GET stream slot. #3221 replaces the plain str() cast with a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` (prefixing `i:`/`s:`) that keeps int and string ids distinct and can never equal `GET_STREAM_KEY`, fixing the same race without those two edge-case bugs.

members.title: fix(streamable-http): reject duplicate in-flight request ids
members.author: Sammy-Dabbas
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3221: Concurrent requests reusing the same JSON-RPC request id overwrite each other's slot in `_request_streams`, cross-wiring responses (one request gets the other's payload, the other hangs). Both PRs add a check to reject a duplicate in-flight request id with an error response.
